location_qualifier: beaches from Kokumbona to Cape Esperance; landings 28 October–8 November
current_activity: beginning of Tokyo Express landings of the regiment
notes: Miller, chapter VII: the Tokyo Express landed elements of the 228th Infantry along the beaches from Kokumbona to Cape Esperance between 28 October and 8 November 1942. The claim date is the first day of that window. Confidence 0.5 (Miller, note 24, cites an Americal intelligence report). Precision 5 km (Kokumbona coordinates are 1-arc-minute rounded).

source_locator: R2225: ch. X, The Capture of Mount Austen
current_activity: holding the Gifu pillbox line as part of Oka's force
notes: Miller, ch. X: understrength battalions of the 228th Infantry were in Oka's Gifu force, with the 124th Infantry and the 10th Mountain Artillery, on the 1,500-yard pillbox line between Hills 31 and 27. Confidence 0.5: Miller only. The regiment remains organic to the 38th Division; the Gifu attachment to the 35th Brigade is CR3798.

source_locator: R2225: ch. X, The Capture of Hill 27
current_activity: making six afternoon counterattacks against Hill 27 after its loss
notes: Miller, ch. X: the Japanese north of Hill 27 launched six infantry counterattacks on the afternoon of 2 January 1943 after the 132nd Infantry took the hill. Identification of the 228th is inferred from Miller's mid-December description of Oka's Gifu garrison (124th and 228th) and is annotated as such. Confidence 0.5: Miller only.

source_locator: R2225: ch. XII, Reduction of the Gifu
current_activity: being destroyed with the rest of the Gifu garrison
notes: Miller, ch. XII: the Gifu was cleared on 23 January 1943 and its garrison almost completely wiped out. Identification of the 228th follows Miller's mid-December description of Oka's garrison and is annotated as an inference. Confidence 0.5: Miller only.
